title: Natural Product Driven Activation of UCP1 and Tumor Metabolic Suppression: Integrating Thermogenic Nutrient Competition with Cancer Metabolic Reprogramming.
one_liner_zh: 综述天然产物激活UCP1产热以抑制肿瘤代谢，涉及分子对接但非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Metabolic reprogramming allows cancer cells to proliferate rapidly, survive nutrient limitation, and resist stress, making tumor metabolism an important therapeutic target. However, pharmacological inhibition of metabolic enzymes often causes systemic toxicity and compensatory pathway activation. To overcome these limitations, recent studies have highlighted an alternative host-centered strategy based on increasing systemic energy expenditure. Recent studies highlight an alternative strategy in which the host increases energy expenditure through uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) dependent thermogenesis, thereby lowering systemic glucose, fatty acid, and nucleotide availability for tumors. Engineered beige adipocytes overexpressing UCP1, PR domain-containing protein 16 (PRDM16), or peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 alpha (PPARGC1A/PGC1A) suppress tumor growth through nutrient competition, suggesting that activating endogenous UCP1 may provide a non-genetic and physiologically aligned anticancer approach. Building on this concept, natural products such as polyphenols, terpenoids, alkaloids, and carotenoids have emerged as promising UCP1 activators that stimulate beige and brown adipocyte thermogenesis through pathways involving AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK), sirtuin 1 (SIRT1), PGC1A, PRDM16, and mitochondrial biogenesis. In parallel, computational studies further indicate that several plant-derived compounds bind directly to the central cavity of UCP1 with high affinity, offering structural support for their thermogenic action. Importantly, many of these compounds also inhibit cancer cell intrinsic metabolism by reducing glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation, lipid synthesis, and amino acid dependent anaplerosis. This review integrates UCP1 biology, natural product mediated thermogenesis, molecular docking evidence, and tumor metabolic suppression, proposing a unified framework in which natural compounds impose coordinated metabolic pressure on cancer through both adipocyte-driven nutrient competition and direct inhibition of tumor metabolism.
abstract_zh: 代谢重编程使癌细胞能够快速增殖、在营养限制中存活并抵抗应激，这使得肿瘤代谢成为重要的治疗靶点。然而，代谢酶的药理学抑制常导致全身性毒性和代偿性通路激活。为克服这些局限，近期研究强调了一种基于增加全身能量消耗的替代性宿主中心策略。最新研究突出了一种替代策略，即宿主通过解偶联蛋白1（UCP1）依赖性产热增加能量消耗，从而降低全身葡萄糖、脂肪酸和核苷酸对肿瘤的可利用性。过表达UCP1、PR结构域蛋白16（PRDM16）或过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体γ共激活因子1α（PPARGC1A/PGC1A）的工程化米色脂肪细胞通过营养竞争抑制肿瘤生长，提示激活内源性UCP1可能提供一种非遗传且生理上契合的抗癌途径。基于这一概念，多酚、萜类、生物碱和类胡萝卜素等天然产物已成为有前景的UCP1激活剂，它们通过涉及AMP活化蛋白激酶（AMPK）、去乙酰化酶1（SIRT1）、PGC1A、PRDM16和线粒体生物发生的通路刺激米色和棕色脂肪细胞产热。与此同时，计算研究进一步表明，多种植物来源化合物以高亲和力直接结合UCP1的中心腔，为其产热作用提供结构支持。重要的是，这些化合物中的许多还通过减少糖酵解、氧化磷酸化、脂质合成和氨基酸依赖性回补反应来抑制癌细胞内在代谢。本综述整合了UCP1生物学、天然产物介导的产热作用、分子对接证据和肿瘤代谢抑制，提出了一个统一框架，其中天然化合物通过脂肪细胞驱动的营养竞争和直接抑制肿瘤代谢，对癌症施加协调的代谢压力。
